title: Regional heat-shielding and connection tiering for dependency isolation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: During multi-region failovers and downstream saturation events we observe connection storms and cascading timeouts that push healthy regions into degraded modes. The existing pooling behavior creates long-lived headroom exhaustion for hotspots and insufficient backpressure to protect latency SLOs. Goal: introduce a lightweight regional 'heat-shield' layer that isolates and shapes traffic to Redis/Kafka/DB dependencies via connection tiering, SLO-driven admission, and graceful degradation profiles. The heat-shield is a thin runtime facade that sits between the request router and dependency clients and implements: 1) multi-tier connection pools (hot/warm/cold) with different admission and TTL policies, 2) SLO-aware admission funnels (token-bucket + per-tenant priority lanes), 3) probabilistic circuit breakers with ramped reconnect and diagnostic sampling, 4) targeted degradation strategies per dependency (stale-while-revalidate for Redis, partial-fetch/slow-path for DB, consumer-priority rebalancing for Kafka), and 5) telemetry for per-tenant/region SLA burn, queue lengths, and shed-rate. This ticket covers the design, prototype implementation for Redis and Postgres read paths, and initial canary rollout under low-traffic Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Design RFC reviewed and approved by SRE/Product/Platform (link included)
Prototype heat-shield library available with Redis and Postgres adapters and feature flags
Automated test coverage for admission logic, circuit state transitions, and tiered pool eviction
Dashboard showing per-region SLO burn, admission drop rate, pool occupancy, and circuit state
Canary rollout on 1 dedicated region with graceful rollback automation
Chaos test run showing reduced cross-region blast radius in simulated downstream slowdowns

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) aggressive shedding reduces latency SLO violations but increases error surface for end-users — we will prefer stale-while-revalidate for cacheable reads to preserve UX. 2) Long-lived pools reduce connect overhead but amplify regional blast radius; tiered pools balance churn and isolation. 3) Per-tenant priority lanes complicate fairness; initial rollout will use conservative per-tenant weights derived from current billing tiers.
